doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: More about his son's tennis and spoiling children
summary: Laws continues the tangent about training his son in tennis, a Bible saying about pampering children, and his son's present family circumstances.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: wake him up to go – he had tennis matches to play. He was in a junior tournament. He won. Up to 14, he did real well, because we were out there practicing more than the average guy, plus he had the advantage of having his own court in the backyard. I found out later, though, you pamper them too much, that’s another saying too. You pamper a person from his youth up, he’ll become a spoiled one.

Yeah, but that’s from the Bible. “Pamper one from his youth up, this one will become a spoiled person.” Now he’s seeing some of the stuff come true. He’s trying to tell me. I couldn’t explain it to him. Now he’s got his own kids. Now he’s bearing the brunt of it.
We saw he can bring the hammer down. So he learned something from Pops. That’s for sure.

Yeah, but sometimes I think he’s a little bit too stringent, when it comes to his kids. You have to have a good reason. There’s no reason for them not to take their little pup with them. That’s not going to hurt anything. There’s some other things that can hurt far worse than that. It wasn’t like she was stealing it. I think it was hers. I think it belonged to her, and she had left it here. She just wanted to take it back. But he’s over there at another place now. He just moved. He’s been here up until about a month ago. But he decided he’d go over there with the mother of his kids.
